What's the gnarliest skateboarding accident you ever had (assuming you have had one)?

Either dropping in on a cement thermometer in the old Flying Wheels skatepark in Alabama or falling at about 45mph on a downhill when my wheel flew off. The thermometer was a huge canyon with a bowl at the end. It had a good 2 foot vert and an additional over vert lip of about a foot. So you literally fell 2-3 foot before your wheels made contact. The first time I tried to drop in (I was about 13yrs old) I head planted and required 10 stitches across the top of my head. The downhill was about 1 1/2 miles long with some curves and we would have someone follow us down at night in a car with their headlights on so we could see. I was riding a Zorlac Metallica board (I know, I'm old). The gullwing trucks I was trying out were a soft ass metal. They would grind great, but it seemed the axles were pretty soft also and they strip out easily. My front right wheel came off about 3/4 of the way down and I couldn't even make it to grass, so I slid and rolled for way too long. That was 25 years ago and I still have a discolored spot on my leg from the road rash. I have had many many other gnarly falls. I started skating in about 1979. I skated almost daily until the 90's. Now I skate once to twice a week. Mostly street and just speed carving and sliding down hills. My knees don't take the impacts of roof drops and big airs like they used to do. But nothing is as good as nice curb, bank or a solid high speed power slide. I guess more mellow than I once was, but I won't stop skating until I am unable or dead. It has gotten me through life to this point. No need to stop now. Apologies for the off subject rant, but I am at work now and it's kinda slow.

TL;DR - I fell. It hurt. Pain goes away, chicks dig scars.

Awesome answer. I find your TL;DR might apply to many aspects of life other than skateboarding as well.

Keep on keepin' on!

It also happened to be an expensive one. The German International is now the clear top-earner at the crisis stricken club BVB.

According to BILD's intelligence, Reus has secured future bonuses of up to €8 Million. He will also receive sponsorship money from Puma and Opel among others. With that, Reus just scrapes the 10 million mark. As of yet, nobody else had earned as much.

Marco Reus is now the richest non-Bayern-Star of the League and matches with the likes of Lahm and Schweinsteiger in terms of salary. Only Franck Ribery has earned more (€10.5 M) in the whole league.
